files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: D. Lindqvist. Complete in sequence; no shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July; some months all runs pay in-month. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and supporting contracts. Check the GL first to prevent a duplicate. If it is missing, book June amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month each prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation according to the fixed asset register, after first verifying what is already in the GL.
5. Compare June vendor-bill documents with GL coding. Verify that each expense account is correct and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, only after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Keystone Freight & Supply began in 2008 when two former warehouse supervisors saw that local businesses needed a dependable source for everyday shipping materials without the complexity of dealing with national catalogs. What started in a borrowed corner of a distribution building grew through practical service, accurate orders, and a willingness to track down awkward items for regular customers.

Today, Keystone Freight & Supply is a small wholesale operation serving manufacturers, repair shops, offices, and regional logistics teams. Its catalog centers on cartons, protective packing materials, labels, warehouse consumables, loading supplies, and other goods that keep shipping rooms moving. The company also coordinates delivery and freight handling when customers need more than a standard drop-off.

The team has a distinctly hands-on character. Sales staff know many buyers by voice, warehouse employees flag unusual order patterns before they become problems, and the back office keeps a close eye on vendor paperwork. Decisions are usually made around a shared worktable rather than through layers of meetings.

The current focus is steady execution: maintaining dependable stock, tightening purchasing routines, improving account follow-up, and making the company easier to do business with. Management is also refreshing its market presence while preserving the responsive, practical service that built the customer base.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Position Keystone Freight & Supply as the practical, responsive wholesale partner for teams that cannot afford delays in the shipping room or warehouse.

## Priorities

- Refresh the brand voice around reliability, product know-how, and straightforward service.
- Update core sales materials so product categories and delivery capabilities are easier to scan.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, focused on packaging choices, warehouse readiness, and common fulfillment bottlenecks.
- Pilot a co-marketing program with a complementary regional partner.
- Build a repeatable customer-story format for email, web, and sales follow-up.
- Re-engage dormant accounts with useful operational content rather than broad promotional messages.

## Quarter plan

### Q3

Finalize messaging, revise the primary product overview, prepare webinar topics, and select the partner pilot. Establish a simple approval process so sales and marketing use consistent language.

### Q4

Publish customer stories, continue the webinar series, evaluate the partner pilot, and refine outreach based on engagement and sales-team feedback.

## Measures

Track qualified inquiries, webinar attendance, follow-up conversations, reactivated accounts, partner-sourced leads, and sales-team use of the refreshed materials. Budget remains pending Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from the previous desk

D. Lindqvist — a few things worth knowing before you close the month:

- The bank's own service fees and charges usually show up near the end of the statement. We have historically picked them up during close, so do not stop the reconciliation early.
- Please scrutinize the June vendor-bill coding. A couple of expenses may be sitting in the wrong accounts, and the supporting documents in `bills/` are authoritative if the ledger description disagrees.
- The Q2 budget was locked in early April. One-off items that arrived in June were therefore never planned, and they are the likely explanation for the larger variances.
- Payroll timing is not automatic here. The pay date for the second monthly run varies, so check the payroll register rather than assuming whether it pays in-month or later.
